children.text: Chamberlain begins the video with a 1-2 second clip making a self-deprecating comment about how she looked in the moment, establishing her unfiltered persona and brand. Chamberlain’s target audience is teenage girls around the same age as her. She pioneered the messy bun, scrunchie, baggy clothes fashion that took over this demographic at the time. Her viewers consciously and subconsciously recreated her outfits and aesthetic and she became a staple of popular culture in the late 2010s. Many YouTubers would introduce themselves in the first couple seconds of their videos by saying something like “hey guys welcome back to my channel” or something similar. Chamberlain spearheaded this type of introduction to establish a casual, trustworthy connection with her audience.

Following Chamberlain’s name title, which introduces typical genre and modality of a vlog, she says “It’s really early, I’m warning you, the beginning of this vlog I’m going to be boring because I’m fucking tired.” She often begins with self-deprecating jokes about herself which became a part of her personal brand. When she says “boring,” she adds a close-up punch-in and a distorting Apple Photo Booth style filter, applying editing affordances that enhance her brand. She often uses these modalities and affordances to add emphasis to something she says. Following that, she uses another punch-in, once on the words “fucking” and “tired.” She did this to emphasize the comedic timing of her self-deprecating joke, using visual and auditory modalities to enhance the delivery.

While explaining that she has only been to Europe once before, Chamberlain includes photos from her trip to Ireland when she was 10 years old and in her "awkward phase.” Chamberlain makes light of her insecurities by using pathos to evoke an emotional response from her audience of similar age young women. Her self-deprecating humor is a factor that her core audience finds endearing. It contributed to the idea that she is just a teen girl that everyone can relate to. She became a ‘friend you are listening to on facetime,’ rather than a typical influencer. Viewers felt as though they could immediately trust her because she was an unfiltered version of themselves.

Chamberlain attended a Paris Fashion Week party and shared an embarrassing event that happened at the party. She mentions how she was too nervous to vlog, and many viewers related to feeling self-conscious when in social situations. She also shows photo proof of her knocking over a decor piece at the elite party she was attending. Including these details allows her audience to connect with a vulnerable moment she experienced, thus strengthening the idea of using pathos to relate a high-fashion branded event to the everyday experience of her viewers. This was one of the first high fashion events she attended, foreshadowing her future success interviewing celebrities at the Met Gala.

Chamberlain ended the video, where she often joked about the fact that she was invited to go to this prestigious event, with a genuine on-screen typed message. Recognizing the exigence of being given the opportunity to attend Paris Fashion Week by YouTube and Louis Vuitton, she made an effort to show her true gratitude. Throughout her words of gratitude she includes preemptive self-disarming messages in parentheses saying she “knows this is corny” and “also corny.” She emphasizes how she has never attended such an event in her life and that she believes it changed her life. She also thanks her audience for their support and expresses how happy it has made her
